subject: Optima Retail — integration priorities and action plan
messages:
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca@optimaretail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform@optimaretail.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: today’s discovery — pain, constraints, initial asks

Thanks for the time today — quick summary from our side and what we need to validate before an internal green light. Appreciated the demo and the discussion about different serving modes.

Key pain points we raised:
- Latency spikes during peak traffic (holiday/promotions window) — 95th pct latency currently ~850ms and sometimes >1.2s for long prompts.
- Token cost unpredictability when reranking large candidate sets — need a way to bound unit economics.
- Ingestion pipeline expects deterministic structured JSON outputs we can drop into our downstream microservices (no manual parsing).
- Our search team needs embeddings + reranking for product search relevance; preference for a batched embeddings endpoint and a rerank API that supports scores + stable IDs.

Initial asks to validate feasibility:
1) Can Redwood support streaming function-calls where we get partial structured JSON as the model emits, so we can begin downstream processing before completion?
2) SDK hooks: we need lightweight client-side retry/backoff + an example for prefix caching / deduping outside of server-side cache.
3) Quantization / model variant guidance: any recommended model/quantization that keeps latency <250ms for short prompts and <600ms for 512-token responses?
4) Compliance question: we attached our security questionnaire — please confirm which items you can answer now vs. need an evidence pack (SOC2/HSM details).

Attach: optima_security_questions.pdf

Next steps from our side: we’ll schedule a demo with our infra and search engineers next Wednesday (Aug 18) if you can provide an engineering-runbook and a short canary plan.

Thanks,
Rebecca
Head of Platform, Optima Retail

---

(Discovery call notes: Optima is migrating search + chat support to a single inference service; estimated weekly requests: 65k gen calls + 120k embedding vectors; peak QPS target ~150 concurrent low-latency requests; regulated PII flows limited to redacted product metadata.)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca@optimaretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: today’s discovery — pain, constraints, initial asks

Rebecca — great to meet your team. Short recap from our side and proposed action items so everyone is aligned. I’ve attached a short post-call note with links to the things Ben and I discussed.

Confirmed pain & goals (from meeting):
- Latency SLO: aim for 95th <300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and tail <700ms for longer generation windows.
- Cost predictability for reranking: use approximate candidate pruning + client-side prefiltering and server-side batched rerank to reduce model calls.
- Deterministic structured outputs required for downstream ingestion; we recommend function-calling + JSON schema validation.
- Embeddings/semantic search: batch embeddings endpoint with stable vector IDs + a reranker that returns scores and chosen canonical id.

Immediate next steps and owners (targets):
- Ben Carter: prepare a short engineering runbook showing a canary plan (GPU pool sizing, fallback to cheaper variant) + latency projections by 2027-08-13. (Ben: can you include an example workload config?)
- Marissa Cole: coordinate an infra/demo slot with Optima’s infra and search teams and own the upcoming demo logistics (target: Aug 18).
- Alex Martinez (me): produce a short SDK patch + example that demonstrates streaming function-calls with incremental structured JSON and a client-side backoff pattern (draft by 2027-08-12).
- Security: We’ll triage your questionnaire — I asked security to mark items that need evidence and which we can answer in-line; expect first pass by 2027-08-11.

Attachments: postcall_notes_optima.md (includes embedded links to a recommended sample request/response for streaming function-calls and a rerank sample).

Questions for you (Rebecca):
- For structured outputs, do you need strict schema enforcement (server-side validation + rejection) or prefer permissive responses with downstream validation?
- Can your infra team provide an anonymized sample of a production request distribution (percent short vs long prompts) ahead of the canary? That will help sizing.

I’ll follow up with the runbook and SDK patch as separate threads. Thanks again — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optima Retail — integration priorities and action plan

Alex — noted. A couple of technical clarifications / asks before I start the runbook draft:
- Streaming function-calls: we should provide both (a) a server-side streaming mode that emits partial JSON chunks and (b) an SDK helper that buffers and validates incremental JSON to avoid partial-parse errors. I’ll prototype an example using the existing streaming frame format.
- Reranking flow: recommend a two-step flow — lightweight candidate scoring model (cheap) to prune to N=30, followed by a full rerank call. This reduces token cost dramatically (rough estimate: 70% fewer full rerank calls).
- Embeddings batching: need to confirm whether Optima prefers per-request IDs or we supply canonical IDs on our side. If they provide stable IDs, we can accept them and return scores.

I’ll include sample configs for GPU pool sizing (p50/p95 latency projections), and an example fallback policy that drops from A100-sized variants to quantized FP16 variants during overloads. Draft by COB 2027-08-13.

Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
